newsitem.title: GREECE: Forex inflows boost liquidity but rates hold.
newsitem.headline: Forex inflows boost liquidity but rates hold.

text.p: Forex inflows of 150 million ECUs and 20 million marks, mainly speculative trades, at the Greek fixing will boost liquidity on Monday but shorts were holding early morning levels in late dealings, dealers said.

"Foreign players sold 150 million ECUs and 20 million marks at the fixing, strengthening the drachma," said a forex trader at a foreign bank. "We are talking basically about speculative flows, but the confidence factor in the economy has also played a role."
Money traders said the inflows would remedy part of the liquidity problem on Monday, but the market could be short for a few more days unless forex inflows continue at a satisfactory pace.
"Shorts are holding morning levels with overnight rates hovering around 13.40 percent," said a state bank trader.
The central bank continued injecting overnight funds at 13.40 percent and provided overnight repos by accepting all kinds of state debt paper as collateral.
The mark was quoted at 157.61/66 drachmas from Thursday's 157.590 fix, the dollar at 241.24/34 drachmas from 241.630 and the Ecu at 300.80/90 from 301.040 drachmas.
